brief: A steel compression spring: 20 mm outside diameter, 2 mm wire, 10 coils, 50 mm free length. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A steel compression spring defined by its coil geometry, intended per the brief to operate without carrying any load.
stated: User states it carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Being a compression spring with specified coil count and free length implies a helical wound geometry with evenly spaced coils
Specifying wire diameter and OD implies an inside diameter can be derived (ID = OD - 2*wire diameter), though end coil behavior affects this
Steel material implies some conventional spring steel, but the specific alloy/grade is not given
unstated: Specific steel grade/alloy (e.g. music wire, chrome-silicon, stainless) and its mechanical properties (shear modulus, yield/tensile strength)
End type of the spring (plain, plain ground, squared, squared and ground) which affects active coil count and seating
Whether the 10 coils are total coils or active coils
Surface finish or coating (relevant for fatigue and corrosion)
Intended installed length or deflection range even if nominal load is zero -- i.e. whether the spring will ever be compressed during assembly or operation
Operating environment (temperature, corrosive exposure, cyclic loading expectations)
Tolerances on OD, wire diameter, free length, and squareness
Why a compression spring is specified at all if no load is ever applied -- the functional purpose of the part is not explained
Spring rate requirement, even if only for verification purposes
Any contact/interface geometry (does it sit in a bore, over a rod, between plates) that constrains its diametral fit
out_of_scope: Selecting a specific steel alloy or spring wire specification
Determining spring rate or stress calculations
Deciding end coil treatment or grinding
Any dimensioning or material choice beyond what was explicitly stated
risk_signals: The brief asserts a compression spring 'carries no load,' but compression springs are definitionally load-bearing elements; this claim is internally inconsistent and should be challenged rather than accepted at face value
If this unstated/unverified load assumption is wrong and the spring is later loaded in service, no load case has been defined, so deflection, stress, and fatigue life are entirely unverified

No information given on whether this spring is part of a larger assembly that could involve personal safety (e.g. mechanism holding a load, safety latch, pressure relief) -- absence of context here is itself a signal worth flagging given the contradictory 'no load' statement

requirements.statement: The spring's overall outside diameter shall be 20 mm, measured across X.
requirements.rationale: The brief states a 20 mm outside diameter; a coil spring is round, so this applies equally to X and Y.

requirements.statement: The spring's overall outside diameter shall be 20 mm, measured across Y.
requirements.rationale: Same outside diameter figure as bounding_box_x, since the part is round about its axis.

requirements.statement: The spring's overall free length shall be 50 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief states a 50 mm free length, which is the whole part's extent along its coil axis (Z).

requirements.statement: The spring wire diameter shall be 2 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief explicitly states a 2 mm wire diameter.
The brief states 10 coils; interpreted as the total coil count for the helical geometry.

assumptions.statement: The spring is made from a generic conventional spring steel (e.g. ASTM A228 music wire or equivalent), since no specific grade is stated.
assumptions.rationale: The brief says 'steel' but gives no alloy or temper; a conventional spring wire grade is the ordinary default for an unspecified steel spring.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a different grade or corrosion-resistant steel was actually intended, the material field would need correction but the geometry is unaffected.

assumptions.statement: The spring ends are assumed plain (unground, unsquared) coils, since no end condition is specified.
assumptions.rationale: No end treatment is given; plain ends are the simplest default consistent with the stated total coil count.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If squared or ground ends were intended, the active coil count and seating behaviour would differ, though since no load case applies this has no functional consequence here.

assumptions.statement: The stated '10 coils' is interpreted as the total coil count (not just active coils) driving the helical geometry.
assumptions.rationale: The brief does not distinguish active vs total coils; total coil count is the natural reading of a bare 'coils' figure in a geometry-only brief.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If 10 was meant as active coils only, the as-built coil pitch and total wire length would differ slightly from intended, though the part would still be buildable.

assumptions.statement: Standard commercial manufacturing tolerances apply to the stated dimensions (OD, wire diameter, free length), since none are specified.
assumptions.rationale: No tolerances are given; ordinary commercial spring tolerances are the conventional default for an otherwise undimensioned brief.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Tighter tolerance requirements, if actually needed, would require re-specification but would not change the nominal geometry.

document.name: Compression spring
document.description: A helical compression spring defined purely by its coil geometry: outside diameter, wire diameter, coil count and free length. No load case applies per the brief.

parameters.description: Overall outside diameter of the spring, across the wire.
Total number of coils, per the brief's bare 'number of coils' figure.
Overall unloaded (free) length of the spring, along its axis.
Diameter to the middle of the wire, derived so the coil's outer envelope matches outer_diameter.
Axial advance per turn, derived so the stacked coils span exactly free_length end to end.

answer.rationale: The part is modelled as a single `coil` feature -- the dedicated primitive for a spring -- rather than a box or cylinder approximation, since the brief gives exactly the parameters that feature wants: wire diameter, turns, pitch and axis. `mean_diameter` is derived from `outer_diameter - wire_diameter` so the coil's wire-to-wire envelope equals the stated 20 mm OD in both X and Y, and `pitch` is derived from `(free_length - wire_diameter) / turns` so the stacked helix spans exactly the stated 50 mm free length without any invented pitch value. Material is left unset because "steel" is a family name only, consistent with the recorded assumption that no specific grade was given; the coil feature is tagged `total` so the total-coil-count requirement reads directly off it.

note: A spring of 10 coils built as one coil of 10 turns, and counted as one coil: `feature_count:coil:total` read the number of coil features. The repair split it into ten one-turn coils joined end to end, the joins left the surface non-manifold, and the spring was held. `answer` is the first design, the one coil of ten turns. `held` is the rerun's design, counted right and then held: its coil drew 13 edges shared by four faces on every grid, the grid's guess on a wire met at a slant.

held.name: Compression spring, 20mm OD x 2mm wire x 10 coils
held.description: A plain-ended compression spring defined purely by its stated geometry (outside diameter, wire diameter, coil count, free length). No load case applies per the brief; pitch is derived from free length, wire diameter and coil count so the geometry stays internally consistent if any of those change.

parameters.description: Outside diameter of the finished coil, across the wire
Diameter of the round wire the spring is wound from
Overall axial length with no load applied

Diameter to the middle of the wire (mean coil diameter), as the coil feature expects; derived so the stated 20 mm outside diameter is reproduced exactly once the wire thickness is added back on each side
Axial advance per turn, derived from free length, wire diameter and coil count so free length, wire size and coil count stay the true drivers of the geometry

requirements.statement: The spring's outside diameter shall be 20 mm, measured across the finished coil in X.
requirements.rationale: The brief states a 20 mm outside diameter; a round part carries this figure in both X and Y.

requirements.statement: The spring's outside diameter shall be 20 mm, measured across the finished coil in Y.
requirements.rationale: Same stated outside diameter, carried in the other horizontal axis for a round part.

requirements.statement: The spring's free length shall be 50 mm, measured along its axis with no load applied.
requirements.rationale: The brief states a 50 mm free length, which is the overall axial extent of the finished part in its unloaded state.

requirements.statement: The spring wire shall be 2 mm in diameter.
requirements.rationale: The brief explicitly states a 2 mm wire diameter.

requirements.statement: The spring shall have exactly 10 coils.
requirements.rationale: The brief states 10 coils as the defining feature count of the spring body.

requirements.statement: The part shall be round about its axis.
requirements.rationale: The brief gives this part's size as a diameter, or calls it round.

assumptions.statement: The spring is made from a generic spring steel (e.g. ASTM A228 music wire or equivalent cold-drawn carbon spring steel), since no specific grade is given.
assumptions.rationale: The brief only says 'steel'; a conventional spring-steel grade is the ordinary default for a compression spring with no stated duty.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A different grade changes modulus, allowable stress and corrosion behaviour, but since the brief states no load case, this does not affect structural verification.

assumptions.statement: The spring has plain (unground, open) ends, as no end condition is specified.
assumptions.rationale: Plain ends are the simplest conventional default when the brief gives only wire diameter, coil count and free length without describing end treatment.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Closed or closed-and-ground ends would change the seating geometry and active coil count, but since there is no load case this has no functional consequence for the stated geometry.

assumptions.statement: The spring operates at ordinary indoor ambient temperature with no corrosive exposure, as no environment is stated.
assumptions.rationale: Default assumption for an unspecified static/decorative application.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Exposure to heat, corrosion or outdoor conditions could require a different steel grade or coating, but does not affect the stated geometric requirements.

assumptions.statement: Standard commercial manufacturing tolerances apply to diameter, wire size, coil count and free length, since none are specified.
assumptions.rationale: No tolerance band is given in the brief; conventional commercial spring tolerances are assumed.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Tighter tolerance needs (e.g. for a precision assembly) would require re-specification, but do not change the nominal requirements already captured.
